rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~85% for 25bp / ~15% for 50bp (CME FedWatch); ECB Dec ~89% (Nov 4); BoJ Dec ~80%; BoC Dec ~34%; BoE 4.00% and RBA 4.85% after November hikes
rows.read: Hotter US inflation figures made a December Federal Reserve hike look all but certain, and some traders now bet on a bigger half-point move. That widens the gap between US rates and most others, which favours the dollar. The Bank of Canada's meeting notes confirmed it is in no hurry, while Japan and the euro area are still expected to hike in December.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: China Oct imports +41.6% y/y (fcst +32%); UK Q3 GDP Thu 1:00 AM CT, fcst +0.7% q/q; euro-area Q3 GDP 2nd estimate Fri 4:00 AM CT
rows.read: No big growth figures landed today; strong Chinese imports overnight were drowned out by the US inflation news. The US economy still looks firmer than Canada's or New Zealand's, a split that favours the dollar. UK growth figures on Thursday are the next real read.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US Oct CPI +0.4% m/m (fcst +0.3%), core +0.3% (fcst +0.2%), third straight +0.3% core; 3-month annualized core ~3.7% (Hercules); Brent ~$92
rows.read: US consumer prices rose faster than expected in October, and the core measure has now run at roughly twice the Fed's goal for three months. That keeps the Fed under pressure and pushes US yields up, which lifts the dollar and weighs on gold. Falling oil eases price fears elsewhere, especially in energy importers.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Dow −0.3%, S&P 500 −0.2% in morning trade (Yahoo Finance); USD/CHF +0.89%, USD/JPY +0.56%, AUD/USD −1.0%, NZD/USD −0.59%
rows.read: US stocks slipped only a little after the inflation figures, so there was no rush into safe havens. That left the franc and the yen weaker as US yields rose. Growth-linked currencies like the Aussie and the kiwi fell the most.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.read: Oil briefly dropped to its lowest since August, then steadied after Iran denied any talks with Washington. Cheaper oil than a month ago lowers the energy bill for Japan and the euro area. Steady prices today gave the Canadian dollar neither help nor harm.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Nov 3: hedge funds for USD, JPY, AUD, GBP; against NZD, CAD, EUR; 4-week change NZD −22K, EUR −34K contracts; next report Friday
rows.read: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and the yen and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro, with big recent additions to bets against the kiwi and the euro. Today's dollar rise went with those bets, so there was no sign of a squeeze. In the Aussie and the pound, hedge funds and real-money investors still sit on opposite sides.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US 10-year auction $42B at 5.020%, bid-to-cover 2.46 (6-auction avg 2.60), indirects 61.2%; 10-year yield ~5.02%
rows.read: Buyers showed little appetite at a US 10-year bond sale, the second weak sale in two days, which helped push long-term US borrowing costs back above 5%. Higher yields support the dollar for now, but weak demand for US debt is a worry to watch. A Democratic Congress still makes President Trump's spending plans harder to pass.
